slides.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a variable-rate Mixture-of-Transformers architecture and a 100-hour tactile-rich dataset to improve robotic dexterity. The approach achieves over 30% higher success rates in tasks requiring delicate force control and deformable object manipulation.

card.one_liner: T-Rex enables tactile-reactive dexterous manipulation using a variable-rate Mixture-of-Transformer architecture and a new 100-hour dataset.
card.key_idea: A three-stage training recipe (human pre-training, tactile mid-training, skill post-training) using a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts to decouple low-frequency visuomotor planning from high-frequency tactile refinement via a VQ-VAE encoder.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 12 real-world contact-rich tasks using a bimanual Dexmate Vega-1 robot; outperformed strongest baselines by over 30% average success rate.
card.limitation: Bottlenecked by hardware issues like sensor distortion, calibration drift, and the lack of dense palm sensing for whole-hand manipulation.

slides.title: ART-Glove: Articulated Tactile Glove for Contact-Grounded Dexterous Interaction Capture
slides.tldr: TACTILE GLOVE FOR DEXTEROUS INTERACTION CAPTURE
slides.highlight: ART-Glove captures synchronized 22-DoF joint measurements and 2048-taxel tactile data to record contact-grounded demonstrations for robot learning.

card.one_liner: ART-Glove captures contact-grounded dexterous demonstrations using rigid functional surfaces and anatomically aligned joints.
card.key_idea: A wearable glove with 16 rigid surfaces, 22 anatomically aligned joints, encoder-based motion tracking, and 2048-taxel piezoresistive tactile sensing for synchronized interaction capture.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via ROM measurements, Kapandji opposition tests, servo-based joint accuracy (sub-degree MAE), and contact-rich tasks (e.g., bottle-cap screwing).
card.limitation: Rigid shells may cause tactile artifacts; current tactile skin only measures normal contact magnitudes and lacks side-surface coverage.

slides.title: Multimodal Physiological Assessment of Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction Under Varying Environmental Conditions
slides.tldr: PHYSIOLOGICAL IMPACT OF ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSORS ON pHRI
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates how operators maintain performance in contact-rich pHRI by increasing physiological effort to compensate for environmental stressors, informing the development of physiology-aware control for RwB.

card.one_liner: Environmental stressors increase operator autonomic workload in contact-rich pHRI even when task performance remains stable.
card.key_idea: A multimodal study using sEMG, EDA, and eye-tracking to decompose operator workload into physical, cognitive, and autonomic dimensions during robot-assisted tracing tasks.
card.evaluation: 12 participants performed tracing tasks under 18 combinations of temperature, noise, and illuminance. Results showed significant autonomic arousal increases with temperature (p < 0.001).
card.limitation: The participant pool lacked industrial pHRI experience, and controlled laboratory settings may not reflect dynamic real-world environmental unpredictability.

slides.title: Inference-time Policy Steering via Vision and Touch
slides.highlight: This work introduces ViTaL, a framework using visual and tactile verifiers to refine robot actions. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception for understanding complex state interactions.

card.one_liner: ViTaL improves contact-rich robot manipulation by combining long-horizon visual mode selection with short-horizon tactile refinement.
card.key_idea: A bi-level optimization framework using a visuo-tactile latent world model, where vision selects the global behavior and tactile-guided diffusion editing refines local contact execution.
card.evaluation: Tested on three real-world tasks (pipetting, wiping, insertion); improved success by 51% over base policy and 33% over unimodal steering.
card.limitation: Performance depends on latent world model fidelity; compounding prediction errors can affect verification of subtle contact events.

slides.title: ROVE: Unlocking Human Interventions for Humanoid Manipulation via Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: RL FRAMEWORK FOR HUMANOID VLA POST-TRAINING
slides.highlight: ROVE enables humanoid manipulation by using reinforcement learning to extract high-value behaviors from imperfect human interventions. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: ROVE improves humanoid VLA policies by learning from imperfect human interventions using optimistic value estimation.
card.key_idea: A RL framework using Optimistic Value Estimation (OVE) and cross-embodiment human videos to extract high-value recovery behaviors from suboptimal, mixed-quality humanoid teleoperation trajectories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-world contact-rich and fine-grained tasks; outperformed SFT and experience-learning baselines (HG-DAgger, RECAP) across multiple rollout-intervention iterations.
card.limitation: Lacks end-effector sensing (tactile/wrist cameras), does not yet handle loco-manipulation, and is primarily an offline/iterative offline RL framework.

slides.title: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning: Self-Aware Policy Execution for VLA Models
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE INFERENCE SCHEDULING FOR VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This framework introduces Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning (EQRL) to dynamically adjust denoising budgets and action chunk lengths based on state difficulty. It reduces inference costs in robot manipulation while maintaining or improving task success.

card.one_liner: EQRL adaptively adjusts VLA inference budget and action chunk length to reduce compute cost while maintaining success.
card.key_idea: A lightweight RL adaptor jointly optimizes latent steering, denoising steps, and chunk length, using critic-ensemble disagreement as a state-difficulty signal to allocate compute.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO, ALOHA, and real robots; EQRL reduced relative NFE by 20-24% in simulation and ~32% on real robots while preserving/improving success.
card.limitation: Offline training lacks causal feedback for different schedules, and the adaptor currently requires per-task fine-tuning without strong cross-task generalization.

slides.title: A Bilateral Teleoperation Framework for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This framework integrates arm-hand coordination and haptic feedback for contact-rich environments, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural skill and aligning human-AI intent via shared control.

card.one_liner: A modular bilateral teleoperation framework for coordinated arm-hand dexterous manipulation with haptic feedback and shared control.
card.key_idea: Integrates a hand exoskeleton and grounded haptic interface with a compliant robotic arm-hand system using position-based retargeting, differential arm control, and multi-scale haptic rendering.
card.evaluation: Validated via a real-world Jenga task (probing, extracting, and placing blocks), demonstrating successful coordinated arm-hand control and stable bilateral operation.
card.limitation: Sensitivity to user anatomy and device donning conditions, causing kinematic estimation errors that require explicit subject-specific calibration.

slides.title: TopoRetarget: Interaction-Preserving Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: TopoRetarget preserves hand-object contact structures during retargeting using a sparse interaction graph, significantly improving RL policy training success and hardware transfer.

card.one_liner: TopoRetarget preserves hand-object interaction during retargeting to improve RL policy learning for dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: It uses distance-weighted Laplacian optimization on a shared interaction graph of hand and object keypoints, incorporating kinematic constraints and penetration handling to maintain local contact structure.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ContactPose, Ho-cap, and Pen-Spin datasets; outperformed baselines in contact precision and improved pen-spinning success by 40.6 percentage points. Zero-shot transfer to Wuji Hand hardware.
card.limitation: Depends on upstream human motion quality and is less effective for 'virtual contacts' where intended interactions lack actual surface touch.
